description: A seed.apply (or seed.restore) the engine refuses — a plan-level refusal, the one case is a downgrade, a lower version than applied — carries the seed's refused code (S43-extra T6, the -31831) and the engine's own sentence verbatim in the data: nothing was written, a downgrade is never silent (SD6), and the operator reads the engine's words, not a summary. The handler maps the engine's untyped refusal to this code and fills the What with its sentence via WithWhat, so the three parts travel unchanged.

data.what: seed: apply of "agents.firstparty" refused: a lower version than applied — a downgrade is never silent
data.means: the engine's own sentence names the refusal — a downgrade (a lower version than applied is never silent), or an apply the engine would not make; nothing was written
data.todo: read the engine's sentence below; a downgrade is refused, never coerced, and a diverged or removed record is re-applied only by `seed.restore`
